text:
Alex: quick heads-up — I hit a weird case with streaming + client cancel yesterday. Node SDK AbortController cancels fine client-side but server keeps generating for ~10s. Observed on hosted API and Dedicated. Anyone seen this?

Mira: hmm. do you have a tiny repro? is this when you abort during the initial headers or while chunks are coming?

Alex: abort while chunks are coming (mid-stream). Repro: Node fetch -> SDK streaming helper -> call controller.abort() after receiving first chunk. Server logs show generation continues; our runtime CPU spikes.

Sachin: interesting. in Go we usually see Read error on body when context canceled, which makes server-side generator see write failures and stop. Node's http/1 keep-alive + chunked streaming may not surface the same error to the app layer immediately.

Alex: exactly. Node client closes, but upstream runtime doesn't get ECONNRESET fast enough. leads to wasted compute and sometimes triggers our retry policy (since the SDK treats client-side abort as a retriable network error).

Olivia: that retry interpretation sounds bad — abort should be final. Where in SDK does retry happen?

Mira: currently retries are folded into the request pipeline middleware. We were treating any non-2xx and some IO errors as retriable. We need to distinguish "client cancelled" vs transient network errors.

Alex: here's the Node snippet I used:

```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const res = await fetch(url, { signal: ac.signal });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
// after first chunk:
ac.abort();
await reader.read(); // sometimes blocks until socket reset
```

And the Go pattern that stops compute: 

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, body)
resp, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
// server sees ctx.Done and request handler sees write errors
```

Sachin: server-side fix options:
- aggressively check for client disconnect via connection close notifications (CloseNotifier / http2 stream close hooks), or check `Write` errors and abort generation.
- on our runtime, add a small write-ahead heartbeat to detect closed pipes faster.

Mira: SDK-side fix options:
- mark AbortController cancellations as non-retriable (special error/mixin).
- when streaming, avoid auto-retry on io.EOF/Abort signals; bubble up a dedicated CancelledError.

Olivia: agree. Also we should doc the expected semantics per language: Node AbortController -> cancel local read and do NOT retry. Go context cancel -> treat same. Add e2e tests across node/go/python.

Alex: I can put together a minimal test harness and PR to change retry rules. Quick question: is there any language where aborting should still allow a server-initiated retry? (i.e., client intentionally aborted but wants SDK to transparently restart)

Sachin: no, that would be surprising. If client requested cancel, we should not restart — that's user intent. The only exception is transparent client-side timeouts where SDK configured auto-retry for idempotent calls, but streaming isn't idempotent.

Mira: +1. plan: 
1) Alex to open PR that: marks controller.abort as CancelledError and treats it non-retriable for streaming endpoints.
2) Sachin to add a small runtime change to detect closed pipes earlier (low-risk kernel-level workaround).
3) Olivia to add language guidance and test matrix (node/go/python) in SDK repo.

Alex: I'll open the PR today and link here — pinging @Mira @Sachin for review. Also adding an e2e that asserts server stops compute within 250ms of client cancel.

zeev-bot: deploy-checker: CI pipeline for PR #5212 queued :eyes: 

Mira: awesome. small nit — please include a short note in CHANGELOG about behavior change and a migration note for anyone relying on old retry semantics.

Olivia: thanks — once PR is up I can draft docs and attach test cases.

Alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/5212 (WIP) — set reviewers @Mira @Sachin. I'll add the hermetic e2e.

Sachin: looked briefly — code looks sensible. I'll run the runtime smoke locally after CI passes. :thumbsup:

Alex: thanks all. will update here with CI status.
